standard_prerequisites.name: Points of a site as morphisms from the topos of a point
standard_prerequisites.use: Represents the given point by a set-valued functor and identifies the topos of a point with the topos of the associated category of sets.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localizing a morphism of sites
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the localized morphism of sites fitting into the commutative diagram of topoi.

core_obligations: Set-up (proof lines 8907-8925): the given point is written as a morphism of topoi from the topos of the associated category of sets, and the localization lemma provides a morphism of topoi between the localized topoi fitting into the commutative diagram.

The functor attached to the element (proof lines 8926-8958): the author uses the identification of the category of sets with the slice over the chosen element, drafts the corresponding continuous functor on the localized site, and verifies that it is the composite of the localized functor with the functor provided by the point.
Conclusion (proof lines 8959-8963): the functor obtained is the one displayed in the statement, so it defines a point of the localized site and fits into the commutative diagram by construction.
proof_roadmap: Represent the point by a set-valued functor and localize the associated morphism of sites.
Use the identification of the category of sets with a slice to produce the functor defining the induced point.
Check that this functor is the displayed one and read off the commutativity of the diagram.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, from a point of a site and an element of the value of the point at an object, a point of the localized site whose stalk is the stalk at the original point of the pullback along the localization (statement lines 8884-8904). The proof is a complete argument: the point is represented by a set-valued functor and the localization lemma gives the localized morphism of topoi with its commutative diagram (proof lines 8907-8925); the author then uses the identification of the category of sets with the slice over the chosen element to produce a continuous functor on the localized site and verifies that it agrees with the composite of the localized functor with the functor coming from the point (proof lines 8926-8958); the conclusion follows by construction (proof lines 8959-8963). The non-formal content is the construction of the induced functor through the slice identification. The claim is H2: a construction with each input named.
